findings.claim: The removed revision ceiling (maxRecordedRevisions) makes the search linear in the memory's current revision. For a page whose body matches but whose frontmatter does not reproduce, every revision from memoryRevision down to 0 builds a rewrite and hashes it. A memory with a very large revision (e.g. billions) makes the migration, including the dry run, appear to hang before it refuses the page as half-migrated.

The old candidate set for an Engram-sourced page also tried an empty revision and an empty kind (revisions ended with "" and kinds with ""). The new loop tries only revisions 0..memoryRevision and kinds {memory type, page's own type}. A stopped run that recorded an entry with an empty revision or an empty type is no longer recognised, and its page is now refused as half-migrated instead of being finished. This regresses recovery that worked before.

Any no-project legacy page now forces exit code 6 on every run, even after a fully successful --apply of all other pages. It also appears in the run of every project, which contradicts 'reported once' for a multi-project vault. Automation cannot tell a clean migration from a failed one until the owner edits that page by hand.

evidence: Reviewed the full diff of the four changed paths. Findings rest on the removed code (the revisions/kinds lists including "", and maxRecordedRevisions) and on the new recordedRewrite loop and the exit-code condition.
